anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: The month-word is to Moses and Aaron; the taking is what is spoken to the people.

pass_a_gloss: For if he had brought on: Speak to all congregation… This month is for you beginning of months, he would have been saying this freely both to Moses and Aaron and to the whole people; but since it is said to Moses and Aaron… and he is commanded to speak not this, but on the tenth of the month that they take a sheep by fathers' houses,
pass_b_english: For if he had added: "Speak to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: This month is for you the beginning of months," (Exodus 12:2–3) he would have been saying this without distinction both to Moses and Aaron and to the whole people. But it is said to Moses and Aaron: "This month is for you the beginning of months; it is first for you among the months of the year." And he is commanded to speak not this, but that on the tenth of the month they should take a sheep according to the houses of the fathers.
source_text: [Εἰ μ]ὲν γ[ὰρ ἐπενη]νόχει· "Λάλη[σον] πρὸ[ς πᾶσαν συ]ναγωγ[ὴν υἱ]ῶν Ἰ(σρα)ὴ[λ λέγων·] Ὁ μὴν οὗ[τος] ὑμῖ[ν ἀρ]χὴ μηνῶν", ἀπ[ο]λελυμέ[νως] καὶ πρὸς Μωϋσῆν κα[ὶ Ἀαρ]ὼν καὶ πρὸς ὅλο[ν] τὸν λαὸ[ν] ἦν τοῦτο λέγων, ἐπεὶ δὲ τῷ Μωϋσῇ καὶ Ἀαρὼν λέγεται· "Ὁ μὴν οὗτος ὑμῖν ἀρχὴ μηνῶν, πρῶτός ἐστιν ὑμῖν ἐν τοῖς μησὶν τοῦ ἐνιαυτοῦ", κελεύεται δὲ αὐτῷ λαλῆσαι <οὐ> τοῦτο, ἀλλὰ τῇ δεκάτῃ|| τοῦ μηνὸς ἵνα λάβωσιν πρόβατον κατ’ οἴκους πατριῶν,
